author: agileacademyinsights
desc: Elon Musk is basically telling his competitors: Go ahead. Copy our rockets. In this interview, Musk says SpaceX doesn't use patents to stop competitors from copying its technology. There's even a rocket outside the company's headquarters that anyone can inspect. Whether copying a rocket is quite that simple is another question. But the leadership question goes beyond protecting a design. Competitors can study a product, understand the technology and hire experienced engineers. Reproducing the way an organization keeps improving is much harder. How do people solve problems together? How quickly can they make decisions? Can teams experiment, learn from failures and apply what they discover? At Agile Academy, we believe those capabilities deserve as much attention as the products they help create. Protecting what a company has already built is only part of the work. Leaders also need to make sure their teams can build what comes next. Catching up with a product is one thing. Catching up with a company that keeps learning and improving is another. Source: Elon Musk, The New York Times DealBook Summit, November 18, 2026. #Leadership #Competition #Innovation

author: jaxdecon
desc: Trigger warning: blood and biohazard cleanup footage. Where do you start when an accident leaves a hotel room covered in biohazard contamination? Thankfully, this person survived and emergency services were able to help. While they’re recovering, I’m stepping into the room for the next six, seven, maybe eight hours to work through the cleanup. This is another side of crime scene cleanup: responding to accidents and medical emergencies that leave behind blood and contaminated materials. Hotel biohazard cleanup doesn’t always involve a crime, but it still requires careful work. The first step on this job is identifying the main source of contamination. Here, that’s the bed. The room might look overwhelming, but having a starting point turns that scene into a process. We begin with bulk removal: removing contaminated bedding and other affected materials, packing the waste into red biohazard bags and boxes, and working through what needs to come out. This is the part of blood cleanup that happens before we can address the surfaces and contamination underneath. Bagging everything up isn’t the end of the job, either. The biohazard waste from this cleanup goes to a dedicated facility for proper disposal. I’m sharing the work behind hotel accident cleanup—from that first walkthrough to removing the biggest source of biohazard. Every room has a different situation, and behind every cleanup is a person whose life was interrupted. Follow Jax Decon for a firsthand look at crime scene cleanup, blood cleanup, and biohazard remediation in Jacksonville, Florida. What would you tackle first walking into this room? #BiohazardCleanup #CrimeSceneCleanup #904
